newsitem.title: USA: AT&T considers legal action against US West.
newsitem.headline: AT&T considers legal action against US West.

text.p: AT&T Corp is considering taking legal action against US West Communications Group for waging what it alleges to be a public campaign against it, a company official said on Friday.
"We're looking at taking possible legal action," said Mark Trierweiler, public relations vice president for AT&T's western region in the United States.

Trierweiler told Reuters that US West had been talking with journalists and public officials in the 14 states where it operated about how AT&T would not invest in rural areas if it were to enter the local market, among other things.
"It's outrageous to say that AT&T wouldn't serve rural customers," he said.
Trierweiler did not specify what kind of action the company might adopt against US West.

Encouraged by the 1996 Telecommunications Act, AT&T and other long-distance carriers are preparing to enter the local telephone market and compete with regional companies like US West, which have had a monopoly in their respective regions for years.
AT&T has already entered arbitration proceedings with US West in a number of the states where US West operates to negotiate how to go about entering it.
A spokesman for US West comfirmed AT&T's allegations about his company's actions, calling it an "education campaign".

"We feel it is appropriate to share the message," he said, explaining how his company did not believe AT&T would act in the interest of the region and bring added value to the local telephone service.

US West and other regional companies like GTE Corp and Southern New England Telecommunications Co tried to get the Federal Communications Commission to stay its new rules designed to introduce competition in the local telephone market.
But the commission rejected their petition last week, saying it did not believe they would be harmed by the rules.

The rules, which the companies are seeking to overturn in federal court, require local carriers to lease space on their lines to new rivals like long-distance companies and cable TV operators at discounts of between 17 percent to 25 percent.
The spokesman for US West said the company did not want to lease its lines at any discount.
"(We would be leasing) our network below its true cost," he said.
